text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tanks and armoured personnel carriers parade in the streets of Sincan, an Islamist-controlled district of Ankara where anti-Western and pro-sharia calls were voiced recently.
- Inflation remains at high levels, failing to move in line with the government's optimism on the economy.
- The Interior Minister suspends the Islamist mayor of Sincan involved in the anti-Israel "Jerusalam Night", where calls were made to implement sharia law in Turkey.
- Twenty-four women are forcibly examined to find out which is the mother of a three-day-old baby who died in a town in the southeastern province of Gaziantep.
- The leftist opposition prepare censure motions to topple the Islamist-led government.
- The general staff headquarters is uneasy about the rise in organisations supporting the introduction of sharia law.
- Clouds of worry hover over the markets as one crisis has followed another since a security scandal broke late last year.
- The speaker of parliament calls on party leaders to unite to solve Turkey's problems.
